t: The principle that allows a life insurer to charge a predictable premium by pooling a large number of similar lives is known as the:
o: Principle of indemnity
Principle of subrogation
Law of large numbers
Principle of contribution
e: With a sufficiently large pool of homogeneous lives, actual deaths converge towards the expected number given by the mortality table, making premiums predictable. Indemnity, subrogation and contribution are general insurance principles that do not apply to life cover.

t: An endowment policy with sum assured ₹4,00,000 and term 20 years has accrued simple reversionary bonuses of ₹45 per ₹1,000 sum assured per year for 12 years when the life assured dies. The death claim (excluding any terminal bonus) is:
e: Bonus accrued = ₹45 × 400 × 12 = ₹2,16,000; add sum assured ₹4,00,000 to get ₹6,16,000. Simple reversionary bonus is calculated on the basic sum assured only.

t: In a ULIP, the investment risk in the investment portfolio is borne by:
o: The insurer
IRDAI through the Policyholders' Protection Fund
The policyholder
The fund manager personally
e: ULIP benefits (other than the guaranteed minimum death benefit) depend on the NAV of the chosen funds, and regulations require every ULIP document to state that the investment risk is borne by the policyholder.

t: In life insurance pricing, the 'net premium' is the premium that:
o: Includes loadings for expenses, contingencies and profit
Is paid after deducting agent's commission
Is calculated using mortality and interest assumptions only, without expense loading
Is net of GST
e: Net (or pure) premium covers only the cost of benefits on the mortality and interest basis; adding expense, contingency and profit loadings produces the gross or office premium charged to the policyholder.

t: The IRDAI Master Circular on Life Insurance Products issued in June 2024:
o: Reintroduced the File and Use procedure for all products
Barred life insurers from selling annuities
Abolished the free-look period
Consolidated earlier circulars and set out norms such as surrender value after the first year and mandatory policy loans on savings products
e: The June 2024 Master Circular replaced numerous earlier circulars and laid down policyholder-friendly norms including special surrender value after payment of the first year's premium, loan facility under all savings products and flexible partial withdrawals in pension plans.

t: A 35-year-old earning ₹10 lakh a year wants the maximum death cover at the lowest premium for 25 years with no return on survival. He should buy:
o: Level term assurance
Endowment assurance
Whole life with limited premium
Money-back policy
e: Level term assurance gives the highest sum assured per rupee of premium because it carries no savings element and pays only on death within the term.

t: Which of the following statements about the human life value (HLV) concept is correct?
o: HLV equals the total premiums an individual can afford to pay
HLV is the present value of the individual's future earnings available to dependants and indicates the amount of life cover needed
HLV is fixed by IRDAI for each income bracket
HLV is relevant only for pension products
e: HLV, developed by Dr S.S. Huebner, capitalises the future income that would be lost on premature death and is the basis for determining an adequate sum assured in protection products.

t: In a joint life endowment policy taken by a husband and wife, the sum assured is normally payable:
o: Only on the death of both lives
Twice, once on each death
On the first death during the term or on maturity if both survive
Only on survival of both to maturity
e: A joint life endowment covers two lives together and pays the sum assured on the first death or at maturity, after which the contract ends; it is popular with spouses and business partners.

t: A pure term insurance policy with a 20-year term pays which of the following if the life assured survives the full term?
o: The sum assured
Total premiums paid with interest
Nothing
A reduced paid-up value
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). A pure term plan provides only a death benefit during the term; there is no maturity or survival benefit, which is why it is the cheapest form of life cover. A return-of-premium variant would refund premiums, but a pure term plan does not.

t: The 'reduction in yield' (RIY) limit prescribed by IRDAI for ULIPs at the end of the fifteenth policy year and thereafter is:
e: IRDAI caps the gap between gross and net yield at 2.25% from the fifteenth year onwards (and 3% at the tenth year), ensuring total charges remain reasonable over the long term.

t: An 'annuity certain for 15 years and life thereafter' means:
o: Payments are guaranteed for 15 years even if the annuitant dies earlier, and continue for life if he survives
Payments stop at the end of 15 years in all cases
Payments start only after 15 years
The annuitant must survive 15 years to receive anything
e: The guaranteed period protects the nominee against early death of the annuitant, after which the annuity continues as a life annuity; the rate is slightly lower than a pure life annuity.

t: Under a hospital cash benefit rider, the benefit payable is:
o: Actual hospital bill up to the sum insured
A fixed daily amount for each day of hospitalisation, subject to a limit on days
Reimbursement of medicines only
The full sum assured on discharge
e: Hospital cash is a fixed benefit product permitted for life insurers; it pays a pre-agreed daily amount (often doubled for ICU) irrespective of actual expenses, usually after a deductible of 24 hours and with annual day caps.

t: IRDAI group insurance norms require that a group formed for the purpose of obtaining insurance:
o: Is acceptable as long as it has at least five members
Must be registered as a trust
Is not permitted; the group must exist for a purpose other than buying insurance
Must be approved by SEBI
e: Group insurance is meant for pre-existing homogeneous groups (employer-employee, bank-borrower, association members); groups formed solely to obtain insurance are not acceptable, as this would amount to anti-selection and mis-selling.

t: Which of the following is a 'loading' added to the net premium while computing the office premium?
o: Mortality rate
Surrender value factor
Bonus rate
Expense and contingency margin
e: Loadings cover initial and renewal expenses, commission, contingency margins and profit; mortality and interest are the assumptions used for the net premium itself.

t: Under Section 80C, premium on a policy issued on or after 1 April 2012 qualifies for deduction only to the extent of:
o: 10% of the sum assured (15% for persons with disability or specified disease)
20% of the sum assured
25% of the sum assured
The full premium irrespective of sum assured
e: For policies issued on or after 1-4-2012 the deductible premium is limited to 10% of the actual capital sum assured (15% under Section 80U/80DDB cases); the 20% limit applies to policies issued earlier.

t: The 'risk premium' for a one-year term cover of ₹10,00,000 on a life whose probability of death in the year is 0.002 is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Risk (natural) premium = probability of death × sum assured = 0.002 × ₹10,00,000 = ₹2,000, before loading for expenses, interest and profit.

t: A 'with-profits committee' of a life insurer is required to:
o: Fix the agents' commission rates
Review the asset share methodology and ensure fair treatment of participating policyholders in bonus distribution
Approve claim settlements above ₹1 crore
Audit the shareholders' fund
e: IRDAI mandates a With-Profits Committee (including an independent actuary and independent director) to oversee asset share computations, expense allocation and the equity of bonus declarations for par policyholders.

t: The minimum guaranteed rate of return on the discontinued policy fund of a ULIP is linked to:
o: The repo rate
The 10-year government security yield
The savings bank deposit interest rate of State Bank of India
The IRDAI-declared bonus rate
e: The discontinued policy fund earns a minimum guaranteed interest equal to the SBI savings bank rate (currently 4% p.a.), with the insurer permitted to charge a maximum FMC of 0.50% on it.

t: Which statement about whole life assurance is INCORRECT?
o: The sum assured is payable on death whenever it occurs
Premiums under ordinary whole life are payable till death or a specified age
Many whole life plans treat survival to age 100 as maturity
Whole life policies cannot participate in profits
e: Whole life plans are available both as participating (with bonuses) and non-participating versions. The other statements correctly describe the product.

t: Under the IRDAI 2024 product framework, a pension policyholder may make partial withdrawals from the accumulated fund for which of the following purposes?
o: Higher education or marriage of children, purchase or construction of a house, or treatment of critical illness
Purchase of a car
Foreign travel
Any purpose, without restriction
e: Partial withdrawals under pension products are permitted up to 25% of the fund value, a maximum of three times during the term, for specified needs such as children's education or marriage, house purchase/construction and critical illness or medical treatment.

t: A combi product in the Indian market refers to:
o: Two life insurance policies bundled by one insurer
A single product combining a life insurance cover from a life insurer with a health (indemnity) cover from a general or health insurer
A ULIP with two funds
A term plan with an annuity option
e: IRDAI guidelines permit a life insurer to tie up with one non-life/health insurer to offer a combi product, with each insurer underwriting and servicing its own component.

t: The Appointed Actuary of a life insurer is responsible for:
o: Marketing of the insurer's products
Approving policy loans
Certifying the premium rates, benefits and reserves of products and the financial soundness of the insurer
Settling disputed claims
e: Under IRDAI (Appointed Actuary) Regulations, the AA certifies pricing adequacy, product terms, bonus recommendations and actuarial valuation, and reports to IRDAI on matters affecting solvency.

t: A policy with annual premium of ₹20,000 and a monthly-mode policy differ in the grace period allowed for payment of renewal premium. The grace period is:
o: 15 days for yearly mode and 30 days for monthly mode
60 days for all modes
30 days for all modes
30 days for yearly, half-yearly and quarterly modes and 15 days for monthly mode
e: The grace period is 30 days for annual, half-yearly and quarterly modes and 15 days for monthly mode; the policy remains in force during the grace period and a death claim is paid after deducting the unpaid premium.

t: Which of the following products would be most suitable for a 58-year-old retiree with a lump sum of ₹50 lakh who wants a guaranteed monthly income for life?
o: An immediate life annuity
A unit linked endowment plan
A 20-year term plan
A money-back policy
e: An immediate annuity converts the lump sum into a guaranteed lifelong income stream, addressing longevity risk; term plans give no survival benefit and ULIPs give no guarantee.

t: A policyholder pays premiums for 6 years on a 20-year endowment with sum assured ₹2,00,000 and then stops. The reduced paid-up sum assured (before bonuses) is:
e: Paid-up value = (premiums paid ÷ premiums payable) × sum assured = (6 ÷ 20) × ₹2,00,000 = ₹60,000; accrued bonuses are added to this reduced sum assured.

t: A ULIP policyholder with regular annualised premium of ₹1,00,000 and age 30 must be offered a minimum sum assured on death of at least:
e: IRDAI requires a minimum death benefit of 7 times the annualised premium for regular premium policies (1.25 times for single premium), so ₹7,00,000; the earlier 10-times rule was reduced in 2019.

t: A guaranteed addition in a non-participating endowment plan is:
o: Declared each year depending on surplus
Equivalent to the terminal bonus
Paid only on surrender
A fixed amount per ₹1,000 sum assured that accrues each year as stated in the policy at inception
e: Guaranteed additions are contractually fixed at the outset (for example ₹50 per ₹1,000 SA per year) and do not depend on the insurer's profits, which distinguishes them from bonuses.

t: Under IRDAI's corporate agency framework as amended in 2022, a bank acting as corporate agent may tie up with a maximum of:
o: Nine life insurers
Three life insurers
One life insurer
Any number of life insurers without limit
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The 2022 amendment raised the ceiling from three to nine insurers in each of the life, general and health categories, widening product choice for bancassurance customers.

t: Which of the following is a correct feature of IRDAI's standard immediate annuity product 'Saral Pension'?
o: It provides a single life or joint life annuity with return of 100% purchase price, with surrender permitted on diagnosis of specified critical illnesses
It offers only a deferred annuity option
It is available only to NPS subscribers
Annuity rates are fixed by IRDAI
e: Saral Pension is a standardised immediate annuity with two options (single life and joint life, both with return of purchase price), a loan facility after six months and surrender on critical illness of the annuitant or spouse.

t: In an employer-employee group term scheme, the sum assured for each member is usually fixed as:
o: An amount chosen individually by each employee after medical examination
A uniform amount or a multiple of salary or grade-based amount, to avoid anti-selection
The outstanding housing loan of the employee
An amount decided by the trade union
e: A formula-based benefit (flat amount, multiple of salary or grade) removes individual choice and limits anti-selection, which is why group schemes can offer cover without individual underwriting up to a free cover limit.

t: A life insurer's Product Management Committee (PMC) must include, among others:
o: A representative of IRDAI
Only independent directors
The Appointed Actuary, Chief Risk Officer, Chief Marketing Officer and Chief Compliance Officer
The Insurance Ombudsman
e: IRDAI requires the PMC to comprise senior functionaries including the Appointed Actuary, CRO, CMO, CCO and others, to review product design, pricing and compliance before launch under Use and File.

t: Under IRDAI norms, a lapsed non-linked policy can be revived within how many years from the date of the first unpaid premium?
o: 2 years
3 years
10 years
5 years
e: The revival period is five years from the due date of the first unpaid premium, subject to payment of arrears with interest and evidence of insurability as per the insurer's board-approved underwriting policy.

t: A couple takes a joint life term plan where the sum assured is paid on the first death and the policy terminates. If both die simultaneously in an accident, the claim payable is:
o: One sum assured, paid to the legal heirs
Nothing, as the policy requires one survivor
Two sums assured
Return of premiums only
e: A joint life first-death term plan pays a single sum assured once; simultaneous death still triggers one payment, which goes to the nominee or legal heirs since neither life survives.

t: When a regular-premium ULIP is discontinued after completion of the five-year lock-in period, the policyholder may:
o: Only surrender and receive the fund value
Choose to revive within the revival period, convert to reduced paid-up, or withdraw the fund value without discontinuance charge
Receive the fund value only after another five years
Continue cover without paying premiums for life
e: After lock-in, discontinuance charges do not apply and the policyholder is given options to revive, continue as reduced paid-up (where offered) or take the fund value; before lock-in the fund moves to the discontinued policy fund.

t: A term rider attached to an endowment policy serves to:
o: Reduce the premium of the base policy
Convert the endowment into a ULIP
Increase the death cover at low cost without changing the savings component
Provide maturity benefit in addition to the base policy
e: A term rider adds pure life cover (payable only on death during the rider term) at a low additional premium, which is cheaper than increasing the sum assured of the endowment itself.

t: Deduction for health insurance premium under Section 80D for an individual below 60 years (self and family) is up to:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). ₹25,000; ₹50,000 where the insured is a senior citizen; an additional ₹25,000/₹50,000 for parents.

t: Under a deferred pension plan with vesting at age 60, if the policyholder dies during the deferment period, the nominee is entitled to receive:
o: Nothing, as the annuity had not commenced
The sum assured of a separate term policy
Only the annuity instalments that would have been paid
At least 105% of the premiums paid (or the fund value, if higher under linked plans), with the option to take it as lump sum or buy an annuity
e: IRDAI requires a death benefit during deferment of at least 105% of total premiums paid for pension products; the nominee may withdraw the entire amount or utilise it to purchase an annuity.

t: The 'free cover limit' in a group term scheme is:
o: The sum assured up to which members are covered without individual medical underwriting
The sum assured below which no premium is charged
The maximum claim an insurer will pay in a year
The number of members who may join without paying premium
e: The free cover limit depends on group size and benefit formula; members with cover above this limit must furnish evidence of health for the excess amount.

t: Which of the following best explains why premium rates for women are often lower than for men of the same age in term insurance?
o: IRDAI mandates a 10% discount for women
Mortality experience shows lower death rates among women at most ages
Women are not permitted to buy large sum assured policies
Women pay a higher GST on premium
e: Pricing follows mortality experience; female lives show lower mortality, which insurers reflect through separate rates or an age set-back, not because of any regulatory mandate.

t: The 2024 regulatory framework requires every individual life insurance savings product to offer:
o: A guaranteed bonus rate
A free annuity option
A policy loan facility, with limits set by the insurer
A minimum return of 8%
e: The Master Circular of June 2024 mandates a loan facility under all life insurance savings products to improve liquidity for policyholders; pure term, pension and ULIP products are treated differently.

t: Which of the following statements about micro-insurance life products is correct?
o: They are available only to persons with income above ₹10 lakh
They require compulsory medical examination
They cannot be sold by LIC
They are simple, low-sum-assured products designed for low-income households and may be distributed through micro-insurance agents such as SHGs and NGOs
e: Micro-insurance products are simplified low-premium life (term, endowment, health) covers aimed at economically weaker sections, distributed through MFIs, NGOs, SHGs and similar entities under IRDAI micro-insurance norms.

t: A 15-year money-back plan of ₹3,00,000 pays 15% of SA at the end of years 3, 6, 9 and 12 and the balance at maturity. The maturity payment (excluding bonuses) is:
e: Survival benefits total 4 × 15% = 60% (₹1,80,000), so the balance 40% of ₹3,00,000 = ₹1,20,000 is paid at maturity together with accrued bonuses on the full sum assured.

t: In a ULIP with 'Type II' or 'Option B' death benefit, the amount payable on death is:
o: Higher of sum assured or fund value
Sum assured plus fund value
Fund value only
Sum assured minus fund value
e: Type I pays the higher of SA or fund value, whereas Type II pays both SA and fund value; mortality charges under Type II are higher because the sum at risk does not reduce as the fund grows.

t: Third-party insurance is compulsory for a motor vehicle used in a public place under which section of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988?
o: Section 140
Section 146
Section 163A
Section 166
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Section 146 makes TP cover compulsory; Section 164 fixes no-fault compensation (₹5 lakh death / ₹2.5 lakh grievous hurt).

t: Why are participating policy premiums generally higher than those of comparable non-participating policies?
o: Because bonuses are guaranteed
Because par policies have no surrender value
Because the premium carries a margin that creates surplus to be returned as bonus
Because IRDAI prescribes a higher premium
e: Par premiums are set on conservative assumptions so that surplus emerges and is shared with policyholders as bonus; non-par products price benefits as guaranteed at the outset.

t: An increasing annuity in which payments rise by a fixed percentage (say 3%) every year is designed mainly to:
o: Give the highest first-year income
Reduce the premium
Return the purchase price faster
Offset the effect of inflation on the annuitant's purchasing power
e: Escalating annuities start at a lower level than a level annuity but grow each year, protecting real income; the starting amount is lower because the insurer funds later increases.

t: Under an accidental total and permanent disability (ATPD) rider, the benefit is usually paid when the life assured:
o: Suffers an accident resulting in permanent loss of use of limbs or sight, rendering him unable to earn a living
Is hospitalised for more than 7 days
Is diagnosed with any illness
Retires at age 60
e: ATPD riders pay a lump sum (or instalments) on permanent and total disability due to accident as defined in the rider, such as loss of two limbs or both eyes; illness and temporary disability are not covered.

t: Under IRDAI norms, if a life assured commits suicide within 12 months from the date of commencement of risk of a non-linked policy, the nominee is entitled to:
o: Nothing
At least 80% of the total premiums paid till death or the surrender value, whichever is higher
The full sum assured
Only the accrued bonus
e: The standardised suicide clause provides at least 80% of premiums paid (or surrender value if higher) for non-linked policies, and the fund value for linked policies, if suicide occurs within 12 months of commencement or revival.

t: 'Profit testing' in product design involves:
o: Checking the agent's commission
Auditing past claims
Projecting future cash flows of a model policy under realistic assumptions to assess whether the product meets the insurer's profit criteria
Comparing premium rates with competitors only
e: Profit testing projects premiums, benefits, expenses, reserves and capital requirements over the policy term to compute measures such as profit margin and internal rate of return, guiding pricing decisions.

t: Premium paid by a company on a keyman insurance (term) policy on the life of its managing director is treated for income tax as:
o: Not deductible
Exempt from tax along with the proceeds under Section 10(10D)
Deductible under Section 80C of the company
Deductible as business expenditure under Section 37(1), with the maturity/claim proceeds taxable in the company's hands
e: Keyman insurance premium is allowed as business expense, but proceeds received by the company are taxable as business income and are specifically excluded from Section 10(10D) exemption.
